problem: VLM-based (cosine-similarity) instruction rewards for embodied RL agents often underperform pure intrinsic-exploration rewards in complex long-horizon environments, because the reward signals are noisy and prior work sidestepped this in simplified settings.
motivation: Encoder-based VLMs are widely used to turn language instructions into dense rewards, but reward noise in complex, long-horizon tasks is understudied. The authors observe that false-positive rewards (rewarding unintended trajectories) mislead agents and cause reward hacking, whereas false negatives merely reduce feedback. Cosine similarity is prone to false positives through state entanglement and composition insensitivity.
key_idea: Reduce false-positive VLM rewards with BiMI, a one-time binary reward issued above a conformal-prediction threshold and scaled down by an instruction-frequency mutual-information term.
insight: Theory (HuRL optimality-gap analysis) shows false positives break heuristic pessimism and leave the bias unbounded, while false negatives preserve the bound. Oracle experiments in Montezuma back this: false-positive and temporally insensitive oracles dropped success to 73.3% and 16.7% versus 100% with no instruction reward. Ablations show Bi alone gives +36.5% and MI adds a further +23% excluding Crafter, and BiMI combines especially well with the intrinsic reward DEIR (e.g., Minigrid Pixl2R 12.4 → 57.7).
method: Binary one-time reward: gives +1 once, only when the VLM similarity p(l_k|τ) exceeds a high-confidence threshold q̂, and then advances the instruction pointer; this avoids accumulating false positives.
Conformal threshold: q̂ is the empirical (lower) quantile at level 1-α (α=0.1) of similarity scores over a calibration set of true-positive trajectory-instruction pairs.
Mutual-information term: p(l_k) is the frequency with which instruction l_k is judged fulfilled in previous-policy rollouts, normalized to a PMF; it downweights signals that fire too often.
BiMI reward: r = max(1{p(l_k|τ) ≥ q̂} − p(l_k), 0), a linearized MI objective following Li et al. 2023.

Noise diagnostics: manipulated pairs (trajectory reversal, instruction negation, order swapping, partial content) plus reward heatmaps and step offsets show that cosine similarity gives false positives.
Combination with intrinsic reward: BiMI's sparse anchor rewards are paired with DEIR exploration rewards; tested with Markovian Pixl2R (CLIP) and non-Markovian ELLM- (X-CLIP/CLIP+RNN) on top of PPO.

setting.backbone: Recurrent PPO (IMPALA CNN + GRU) with fine-tuned CLIP / X-CLIP reward models
setting.training_data: VLMs contrastively fine-tuned on ~80k instruction-observation pairs each for Minigrid and Crafter (auto-annotated from engine state), ~300 manually annotated pairs for Montezuma; RL trained for 1M frames
setting.observation: pixel frames (single frame or short trajectory snippets) plus language instruction sequence
setting.simulator: Crafter, Atari Montezuma's Revenge, Minigrid 'Go To Seq'
setting.privileged: engine internal state used to annotate VLM fine-tuning data and compute the score metric (and for oracle reward experiments); none for the BiMI agent at test time

numbers_note: No standard embodied-navigation benchmarks; results are on Montezuma, Minigrid Go To Seq and Crafter RL environments (score metric), so no entries fit the canonical benchmark list.
results: VLM rewards without noise handling underperform the DEIR intrinsic baseline by 27–49% (Table 1). BiMI raises Pixl2R by 67% on average and ELLM- by 22%. BiMI + DEIR gives Montezuma 0.267/0.279, Minigrid 57.7/56.2 and Crafter 11.0/13.1 (Pixl2R/ELLM-), beating DEIR alone (Minigrid 55.5, Crafter 19.7 is not beaten, since DEIR alone stays higher on Crafter). BiMI alone hurts Crafter (−15%/−12%) due to repeated survival subtasks.
limitations: Only linear sequences of instructions were studied; conditional or ambiguous instructions are excluded.
The theory is not rigorously extended to non-Markovian reward models, and the MI term hurts Crafter, where subtasks must be repeated.
Requires a calibration set of true-positive pairs and fine-tuned VLMs; not tested on real navigation benchmarks or robots.
